title: Rule
description:
One engineering rule, as its TOML file states it.

Enforcement is derived from [`Consequence`] and [`Lifecycle`], never
stated: a trial rule only reports; an enforced business or containment
finding blocks; an enforced coherence finding accrues debt and never
blocks. This crate holds no verdict logic.

check_class.description: How the rule is held: exactly, approximately, or by a reviewer.

checks.description:
The checks that hold the rule. A trial or enforced rule has at least
one unless its class is judgement.

consequence.description:
What it costs when the rule does not hold. Set by the owner at
registration, revisable through the lifecycle.

contracts.description: Files whose types the code must satisfy, relative to the mount.

exemplars.description: Real files that show the rule followed, never copies.

id.description:
`rl-NNNN`: opaque, never renumbered or reused. The file is
`rules/<id>.toml`.

patterns.description: Names of the patterns this rule belongs to. Written by the lab.

scope.description: Where the rule applies within the mount that selects it.

source.description:
The numbered rule in a repo's `engineering/` this rule restates.
Transitional: retires when `gauge plan` renders and the rule text
moves into the registry.

tags.description: Free descriptive strings. Never an enforcement input.

why.description: The reason, as prose. Rendered for the agent on demand, not by default.

Check.description: One thing that holds a rule or detects a deviation from a heuristic.

precision.description:
For an approximate check, the measured precision as a fraction,
once the lab has one.

ref.description:
What the kind needs to find the check: a lint rule name, a file, a
script, or the text a reviewer is given.

CheckClass.description:
Exact fails on every breach and only on a breach. Approximate emits a
signal with known imprecision. Judgement is a reviewer grading against
the statement.

CheckKind.description: The adapter a check runs through.

Consequence.description:
What a rule costs when it does not hold. A trial rule only reports,
whatever its class.

oneOf.description: A violation changes what a user experiences. Enforced findings block.

A violation weakens the sandbox or the repo's security: governance
files, CI permissions, secrets. Enforced findings block and never
become debt.

A violation breaks architecture or a convention without changing
behaviour. Enforced findings never block; they accrue debt.

Lifecycle.description:
Draft is written, trial reports without consequence, enforced counts,
retired is kept so old findings and suppressions still resolve.

reason.description: Why the entry entered its current state. Required when retired.

renamed_from.description: Earlier ids, so a stale suppression can be rewritten.

replaced_by.description: When retired, the ids that took its place.

since.description: The date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, the entry entered its current state.

until.description:
When retired, the date suppressions stop resolving. Absent means
kept indefinitely.

Scope.description:
Where a rule or heuristic applies. Which repos and app types it applies
to is decided by the profile nodes that select it, and the runtime by
the runtime leaf's platform; this narrows within a mount.

exclude.description: Globs relative to the same mount, taken out of `paths`.

paths.description: Globs relative to the mount of the node that selects the rule.

Source.description:
A pointer into a repo's `engineering/`: the file, relative to the repo
root, and the rule's number in it.
